notes: Part B (ordinary/business) income is taxed at 5%. The 4% surtax applies to total taxable income above $1,107,750 for tax year 2026 (inflation-indexed; $1,083,150 in 2025); the threshold is the same for single and joint returns. Folded in as 9% above the threshold.
Massachusetts has no standard deduction; personal exemptions are $4,400 single/MFS, $6,800 HoH, $8,800 joint (plus $1,000 per dependent, $700 age 65+, $2,200 blindness - not modeled).

Base is Massachusetts Part B income: business profit with only Massachusetts-allowed deductions. The deduction for Social Security/Medicare/self-employment tax paid (up to $2,000 per person, Form 1 line 11) is modeled for the self-employed person; a spouse's own FICA deduction is not.

Not modeled: 8.5% short-term capital gains rate, 12% collectibles rate, rental deduction (50% of rent up to $4,000), No Tax Status and Limited Income Credit, child and dependent credits, and Massachusetts EITC.
Massachusetts did not adopt several 2025 federal (P.L. 119-21) business changes (e.g., IRC 174A R&E expensing); differences in business depreciation/expensing are not modeled.

seDeduction.note: Massachusetts does not allow the federal half-SE-tax adjustment. Instead it allows a deduction for Social Security, Medicare and self-employment tax paid, up to $2,000 per person (Form 1, line 11); modeled for the self-employed person.

seHealthInsurance.note: Allowed on Schedule Y, line 7, equal to the federal self-employed health insurance deduction.

retirementContributions.note: Form 1 instructions: payments to an IRA, Keogh, SEP or SIMPLE account are not deductible for Massachusetts income tax purposes.

qbi.note: Massachusetts uses its own income definition and has no QBI deduction.

localIncomeTax.note: Massachusetts cities and towns do not levy a local income tax.

estimatedTax.threshold: Expected tax due of more than $400 on income not subject to withholding
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: Pay at least 80% of the current year's tax (66.67% farmers/fishermen) through withholding and estimates, or pay at least 100% of the prior year's tax (prior return must cover a full 12 months) divided among the installments; no penalty if tax due after credits and withholding is $400 or less (Form M-2210). Taxpayers subject to the 4% surtax must file and pay electronically.

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $500 Certificate of Organization (M.G.L. c. 156C, s. 12; 950 CMR 112.00)
businessCosts.annualReportFee: $500 annual report, due each year by the anniversary date of the original certificate (M.G.L. c. 156C, s. 12)
businessCosts.franchiseOrMinimumTax: None for a sole proprietor or single-member LLC taxed as a disregarded entity (the Massachusetts corporate excise applies to corporations)
